findings.F1: The Calmar failure comes from the book's falls riding the coins' own declines. The chained book returns 26.8 % a year, but its deepest fall is 48.1 %. Its five deepest falls (48 %, 44 %, 42 %, 35 %, 34 %) each last 157 to 611 days. In each, the coins' own chained return to the trough is -37 % to -81 % (-81 % in the deepest, troughing in w14).
findings.F2: The book is almost always long: 91 % of all bars. It is long on 98 % of "trending" bars and still on 83 % of "unknown" bars, where the 3-day return is not positive and the forecast is 0. The 72-bar minimum hold keeps it long there, so it carries most of each coin decline.
findings.F3: The book's hourly gain is concentrated in coins whose 30-day return is positive.
findings.F4: On the 72-bar grid, the idea's effect appears only with a positive 30-day return.
findings.F5: Across all positive-forecast cases, the efficiency effect is graded only at its top. Excess 72-bar returns by efficiency quintile run -0.51 %, -0.22 %, -0.10 %, +0.20 %, +1.16 % (top t 2.87, 573 cases each). The idea's overall unusual move is -0.13 % per case, so most of the forecast range sizes the book on noise.
findings.F6: Efficient rises close to the 30-day high continue most. In the top third of efficiency and the nearest third to the 30-day high, the excess 72-bar move is +1.44 % (t 2.80, 369 cases). Far from the high it is +0.43 % (t 0.70, 168 cases).
findings.F7: The 30-day return grades the next 72-bar move among positive-forecast cases. Excess returns by 30-day-return quintile are -0.11 %, +0.13 %, +0.12 %, +0.40 %, +0.62 %. In the lowest quintile, 26 % of cases fall more than 5 % over the next 72 bars, against 15 % in the middle quintiles.

ideas.idea: The more efficiently a coin has risen over its past 3 days (its 3-day rise large relative to the sum of its absolute hourly moves), the more it keeps rising over the next 3 days, only while its 30-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: An efficient 3-day rise is a reason to be long only inside a coin's 30-day uptrend; in a 30-day downtrend it is a reason to stay out, which removes the exposure that carries the deepest falls.
ideas.name: efficient rise within uptrend

ideas.idea: The more efficiently a coin has risen over its past 3 days, the more it keeps rising over the next 3 days, the more so the closer its price stands to its highest close of the past 30 days.
ideas.consequence: An efficient rise that pushes into new 30-day highs is a reason to be long and larger, while one far below its 30-day high is a weak reason.
ideas.name: efficient rise near highs

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 30-day rise, the more it rises over the next 3 days.
ideas.consequence: A coin's 30-day trend is a reason to be long in proportion to its rise, and a reason to refuse longs when it has been falling for a month.
ideas.name: thirty-day trend continuation
